newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli ministries lock horns over milk imports.
newsitem.headline: Israeli ministries lock horns over milk imports.

text.p: Israel's Agriculture Ministry locked horns with trade officials on Monday over a decision to allow the duty-free import of up to 100 million litres (26 million U.S. gallons) in dairy products.

A ministry spokesman threatened to stop issuing licences for importing agricultural products until trade authorities reversed the decision to allow imports of powdered milk and other dairy products mainly from Europe and the United States.
"We will fight this to the very end. As long as they don't impose the tax we will not give licences for the import of other agricultural goods to Israel," spokesman Naftali Yaniv told Reuters.
Yaniv said the decision to allow the imports, made more than a year ago and coming into effect only now, would make it hard for Israeli dairy farmers to compete with products from abroad.
He said 100 million litres equalled about 10 percent of Israeli dairy production.
A few dozen dairy farmers brought calves to the Industry and Trade Ministry on Monday and staged a vigil outside to protest against the imports.
An official at the Industry and Trade Ministry said the duty-free import was anchored in bilateral free trade area (FTA) trade agreements and could not be reversed.
